headline: After the fix (node --test ✖ recognised, repeated failures folded) trimming fires on all 5 tasks. Haiku 5.5 subagents still pass 20/20 in both arms, and total session tokens drop 18% (4.96M → 4.04M): js-one-bug −49%, dotnet-build −35%, js-three-bugs −25%, while js-root-exception (+8%) and js-feature (+24%) went up by about the run-to-run noise. Try it on real work before adopting.

arms.name: Claude + trim-core (Jev live, rules fallback)
arms.engineVersion: typesafe/jev-1.13 via OpenRouter decisions API, minJevConfidence 0.6

evaluation.tokenScope: all tokens of the subagent's whole task session (input + output + cache read + cache write)
deviations: Same harness as 20261017-sct-agent-01 (not the real hook: both arms run tests through run.mjs; A raw, B through trim-core.ts decideAndBuild with Jev live). The hook's deny-shape for failed commands is not reproduced.
Jev was asked only on dotnet-build (errors_only / errors_and_warnings); the node tasks are trimmed by rules alone, so the gain there is the rules, not Jev.
Noise: the previous run showed ±17% between arms on untrimmed tasks, so the +8% and +24% cases are not clear regressions; js-feature B took one or two more turns in both reps, worth watching.
Output Claude reads per test run: node tasks 11–74 KB → 1–12 KB, dotnet 238 KB → 7–9 KB.
Tokens include cache reads (~85% of all tokens, billed at ~10% of input).

Synthetic tasks with obvious bugs (make_tasks.mjs), 2 reps, one model (haiku, effort xhigh). Some agents briefly wrote scratch files outside their folder and deleted them; grading re-ran the raw command and checked protected files.
